01 Honest Run.goal: The reference behaviour of the available chain with no faults.
01 Honest Run.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency, k = 4, c = 2. Nothing is ever finalized.
01 Honest Run.result: Nodes vote as soon as the proposal arrives, about 0.2 s into the slot, and 3/4 of the committee confirm it optimistically within the slot: the confirmed tip is the head. That confirmation also fast-locks the block, so at the end of every slot the anchor, the deepest lock, is the head itself.

02 Two-Slot Cut 50/50.goal: The shortest even split that costs a confirmed block.
02 Two-Slot Cut 50/50.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency, k = 4, c = 2. Nodes 0–1 and 2–3 are cut apart for slots 48–49.
02 Two-Slot Cut 50/50.result: Side A holds slot 48's block with its own 32 votes, exactly n/2, so it confirms the block and fast-locks it. Side B does not see that block during the cut. After the heal the lock moves back, and side A loses the confirmed block at slot 52. Heads agree 2 slots after the heal.

03 Partition 50/50.goal: What an even split does to confirmations and locks, and how the chain heals.
03 Partition 50/50.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency, k = 4, c = 2. Nodes 0–1 and 2–3 are cut apart for slots 48–63.
03 Partition 50/50.result: Each half confirms and fast-locks its own branch with 32 votes, exactly n/2, so the two halves hold conflicting locks through the cut. After the heal the votes split 32–32, no child of the last common block has a strict majority, and both branches are discarded: 7–8 confirmed blocks per node are orphaned. Heads agree 3 slots after the heal, and no conflicting lock outlives the cut.

04 Partition 75/25.goal: A split with a clear majority on one side.
04 Partition 75/25.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency, k = 4, c = 2. Node 3 is cut off from nodes 0–2 for slots 48–63.
04 Partition 75/25.result: The 48-validator side keeps confirming as if nothing happened. The lone node confirms its own blocks, a strict majority of the 16 voters it sees, and loses 3 of them at the heal. Heads agree in the heal slot.

05 Partition 52/48.goal: A near-tie: one side with slightly more than half of the validators.
05 Partition 52/48.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency, k = 4, c = 2. Nodes 0–1 (33 validators) and 2–3 (31) are cut apart for slots 48–63.
05 Partition 52/48.result: At the heal the 33 side's branch wins and the 31 side loses 7 confirmed blocks. Heads agree in the heal slot.

06 Long Partition 50/50.goal: A 64-slot even split: does the damage stop growing with the length of the cut?
06 Long Partition 50/50.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency, k = 4, c = 2. Nodes 0–1 and 2–3 are cut apart for slots 48–111.
06 Long Partition 50/50.result: The same outcome as the 16-slot cut, scaled up: both branches are discarded, and every block confirmed during the cut is lost, 28–35 per node. Heads agree 2 slots after the heal. The locks cap nothing here: each lock lives at most k slots, so none is left from before the cut.

07 Messy Heal.goal: The 50/50 cut, with the held messages trickling out over two slots after the heal.
07 Messy Heal.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency, k = 4, c = 2. Nodes 0–1 and 2–3 are cut apart for slots 48–63; each held message arrives up to 12 s after the heal.
07 Messy Heal.result: The same outcome as the clean heal, one slot later: heads agree 4 slots after the heal, and 8 confirmed blocks per node are orphaned. Side A's head switches four times while the messages trickle in.

08 Three-Way Cut.goal: A cut into three groups: half of the validators together, and the other half split in two.
08 Three-Way Cut.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency, k = 4, c = 2. Nodes 0–1 (32 validators), node 2 (16) and node 3 (16) are cut apart for slots 48–63.
08 Three-Way Cut.result: Every group confirms its own blocks. At the heal the half's branch wins, and the two single nodes lose 5 and 3 confirmed blocks.

09 Two Cuts in a Row.goal: A second cut before the chain has settled from the first.
09 Two Cuts in a Row.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency, k = 4, c = 2. Nodes 0–1 and 2–3 are cut apart for slots 48–55; then node 3 is cut off from nodes 0–2 for slots 60–67.
09 Two Cuts in a Row.result: After the first heal both branches are discarded, as in the 50/50 cut: side A loses 3 confirmed blocks and side B 4. In the second cut node 3 loses one more. Heads agree in the second heal slot.

10 Half the Network Asleep.goal: Half of the validators asleep for 16 slots, then a restart and a rejoin.
10 Half the Network Asleep.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency, k = 4, c = 2. Nodes 2–3 sleep through slots 48–63.
10 Half the Network Asleep.result: The awake half keeps confirming: it needs a strict majority of the voters it sees, not of all validators. Blocks are missing only in the sleepers' proposal slots. The sleepers restart, join a slot later, and nothing is orphaned.

11 Three Quarters Asleep.goal: Only a quarter of the validators online: the regime where the finality gadget could not help.
11 Three Quarters Asleep.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency, k = 4, c = 2. Nodes 1–3 sleep through slots 48–63.
11 Three Quarters Asleep.result: Node 0 alone keeps a confirmed chain. The chain grows only in node 0's own proposal slots, and each of its blocks is confirmed one slot later. After the wake the sleepers adopt that chain and nothing is orphaned.
